title: How far does the JARVIS look reach beyond the live map?
context: The live map strip is full HUD (cyan glass, mono labels, corner brackets, scan lines); the rest of the hub is a calm messaging app, so the two halves read like different products. You asked for a futuristic JARVIS look at maximum polish. Readability of long messages and cards must not suffer. Found in the ux-review round.

options.name: HUD frame, readable content
options.summary: The shell takes the HUD language: sidebar and headers get cyan hairlines and glow edges, cards waiting on you get corner brackets, labels become small mono capitals, decision options get hexagon keys, a short boot sequence on load, a lock-on flash when a notification opens a card. Message and card text stays in the normal sans font at full contrast.
pros: One product from strip to composer
Long text stays easy to read
cons: Needs care so brackets do not clutter long threads
options.effort: Large, in two or three passes

options.name: Full HUD everywhere
options.summary: Everything in the HUD style, including mono text for messages and a glass background over a live grid.
cons: Mono body text is slower to read on a phone

options.name: Keep the HUD in the map
options.summary: Only small touches outside the map (focus rings, link light).
cons: Two visual languages stay side by side

recommendation: It carries the map's look into every frame you touch while keeping what you read in a readable font; the desktop and phone mockups from this round show it.
